items.title: Foreign or local? Investors at lossover GIFT funds
items.description: Investors are grappling with confusion when it comes to reporting GIFT City fund investments in their tax returns. Fund houses provide varying guidance on whether these should be categorized as foreign assets. While GIFT City falls under the foreign category per FEMA regulations, it's treated as a domestic entity for income tax.

items.title: Tata, SP Group explore share swap to unlock Tata Sons stake amid valuation divide
items.description: Tata Sons and the Shapoorji Pallonji Group are currently negotiating the monetization of a stake but are at an impasse concerning the transaction's structure and valuation. Among the options discussed is a share-swap deal. The SP Group is eyeing this opportunity to tackle its significant debt. Their recent refinancing attempts indicate a solid confidence level in the pledged Tata Sons shares.

items.title: HSBC offers 19x FCNR(B) leverage in GIFT City
items.description: HSBC's GIFT City unit offers NRIs significant leverage on FCNR deposits.  An NRI can borrow up to nineteen times their own funds for deposits.  This special deposit program attracts overseas dollar deposits and boosts inflows.  The Reserve Bank of India temporarily relaxed interest rate ceilings for this purpose.  This initiative aims to attract foreign exchange until September 2026.

items.title: MSCI rejig could bring $2.3 billion into Indian stocks
items.description: An upcoming MSCI index rebalancing may introduce about $2.3 billion in passive investment flows.  The global index provider will announce changes on August 12 after market close.  Several Indian stocks are likely candidates for inclusion in the MSCI India Standard Index.  These changes will impact index-linked exchange-traded funds and mutual funds.  The rebalancing will become effective for portfolios on August 31.

items.title: Stock Radar: Bajaj Finance inching higher after brief consolidation; time to buy?
items.description: Bajaj Finance stock shows bullish momentum after a period of consolidation. Experts suggest buying for a target of 1,100 levels in coming weeks. The stock has been making higher highs and higher lows since June. It is currently trading above key moving averages on daily charts. Analysts recommend a target of Rs 1,100 with a stop loss below Rs 1,000.

items.title: Private insurers seek tweaks in unlisted investment plan
items.description: Private insurers want Irdai to change proposed investment norms for unlisted companies. They suggest linking exposure limits to shareholders' funds instead of surplus. This change could unlock billions for investment in privately held businesses. The proposed framework may expand sector investment capacity significantly. Insurers seek greater flexibility in managing investment portfolios.

items.title: RBI bars banks, NBFCs from selling acquired stressed assets back to defaulting borrowers, related parties
items.description: New Reserve Bank of India norms will prevent lenders from reselling acquired assets to defaulting borrowers. These prudential rules apply to banks, small finance banks, and NBFCs starting October 2026. Specified non-financial assets are those obtained when resolving stressed loans from borrowers. Lenders must establish board-approved policies for acquiring and disposing of these assets. These assets will be disclosed separately on balance sheets, not as NPAs.

items.title: Deepfake scam rattles Sky Gold as subsidiary suffers Rs 11 crore loss after unauthorised fund transfer
items.description: Sky Gold and Diamonds' shares may remain under pressure after its subsidiary, Starmangalsutra Private, reported a Rs 10.70 crore fraud involving deepfake techniques. Fraudsters allegedly gained unauthorised access to a company-issued mobile phone and laptop, impersonated a director, and tricked an employee into transferring funds to unknown bank accounts. The company has reported the incident to cybercrime authorities and banks.

items.title: UPL among 5 stocks that closed above VWAP, signaling bullish shift
items.description: On July 16, the closing prices of five stocks in the Nifty500 pack rallied over 1% relative to their VWAP (Volume Weighted Average Price). A shift above the VWAP suggests a potential bullish trend, according to stockedge.com's technical scan data.When the closing price rises above the VWAP, it signifies that the closing price is higher than the average price at which it was traded throughout the day, with the average being weighted by trading volume. This occurrence is often interpreted as a potential bullish signal by traders and investors, which could indicate positive sentiment in the market.

items.title: IIFL Finance among 3 stocks flashing bullish signals, hinting at a possible uptrend
items.description: On July 16, three stocks in the Nifty500 appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.Represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and a small or nonexistent lower shadow, it indicates strong buying pressure throughout the session. Traders interpret it as a signal that buyers were in control from the opening to the closing, often using such patterns for informed decisions about future price movements in financial markets.

items.title: D-St set for a cautious opening as GIFT Nifty signals muted start
items.description: Indian benchmark indices opened positively but traded within a narrow range. Market participants remained cautious due to the weekly Sensex expiry and intraday volatility. Analysts expect the index to hold support and witness a pullback towards higher levels. Foreign portfolio investors net sold shares while domestic institutional investors were net buyers.
